verdict.rationale: NVIDIA documents official SDKs that target RTX GPUs. The CUDA Toolkit ships with a compiler, runtime, GPU-accelerated libraries, Nsight tooling, and C++/Python tile-programming interfaces, and the RTX Neural Shaders SDK uses Tensor Cores. Independent Phoronix CUDA/OptiX benchmark runs show these SDKs working on the 5090. missing for 10: an explicit RTX 5090/Blackwell support statement in the SDK docs, and hands-on developer reports of building against the SDKs (as opposed to running benchmarks).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The NVIDIA® CUDA® Toolkit provides a development environment for creating high-performance, GPU-accelerated applications.
The toolkit includes GPU-accelerated libraries, debugging and optimization tools, a C/C++ compiler, and a runtime library.
It is built on top of the CUDA Tile IR specification and allows you to write tile kernels in Python.
The RTX Neural Shaders SDK lets developers train shader data on an RTX PRO workstation and accelerate neural representations with NVIDIA Tensor Cores at runtime.
across 60+ CUDA/OptiX/OpenCL/Vulkan benchmarks the 5090 delivered 1.42x the RTX 4090's performance.
